dict.string: Search and control Aqara devices and scenes

# alfred-aqara
Control Aqara devices and run saved scenes from Alfred. Inspired by Alfred home automation workflows, with the same device-first command style.
This version uses **Aqara Agent's official cloud API**. Your Hub M3 and its devices must be registered in Aqara Home. The Mac needs internet access; the hub's IP address and a Home Assistant installation are not required. Availability depends on the devices and account region exposed by Aqara Agent. This is not a direct LAN or Matter controller.
## Requirements
- macOS with Alfred 5 and a Powerpack license. - Python 3.9 or newer, installed from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/macos/) or Homebrew (`brew install python`). No Python packages are required. - An Aqara account that can sign in to [Aqara Agent](https://agent.aqara.com/login).
## Install and connect
1. Build the workflow with `python3 workflow-build`, then open `dist/Aqara-0.2.6.alfredworkflow` to import it into Alfred. 2. Type `aq login` in Alfred and press Return. Sign in with your Aqara account. 3. Copy the **aqara_api_key** shown on the page. Type `aq apikey` in Alfred and press Return to paste it into the secure dialog. It is saved in macOS Keychain. The key is never entered in Alfred's search field or stored in the workflow. 4. Run `aq update`. If the account has one home it is selected automatically. With multiple homes, use `aq home` to select one; that selection refreshes its devices and scenes. 5. Type `aq` to browse, or start typing a device, room, or scene name.
macOS may ask you to allow Python to access the Aqara Keychain item. After replacing or updating Python, you may need to allow access again.
## Commands
Command choices have distinct titles such as “Turn on,” “Turn off,” and “Set brightness,” with the device, account, and home in the subtitle. A search matching a single device opens its command list, including when you type only part of its name.
Tab completes the full device name and command. Commands needing a value keep a trailing space so you can continue typing. Mode and colour commands suggest values, and completing a numeric command preserves the value you entered. For example, `aq Desk dim 50` can resolve a unique `Desk Light` and autocomplete to `Desk Light dim 50`. Duplicate device matches require selecting the exact device before a command can run.
Pressing Return on a control sends it to Aqara. Status rows display the device name as the title and the readings as one subtitle line; selecting a status row returns to that device's command list. Use `aq showstatus on` to show the summary above the commands whenever a single device is selected. Names containing spaces, quotes, or shell punctuation are supported.
| Command | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `aq <search>` | Search device names, rooms, device types, and scenes | | `aq <device> status` | Read current state (also works for sensors and hubs) | | `aq <device> on` / `off` | Power controls for lights, switches, outlets, and ACs | | `aq <light> dim 50` | Brightness, 1–100%; use `off` to turn the light off | | `aq <light> color blue` | Set a named color, where supported | | `aq <light> ct 4000` | Color temperature, 2700–6500 K, where supported | | `aq <curtain> open` / `close` / `stop` | Open, close, or pause a curtain/shade | | `aq <curtain> slevel 50` | Opening percentage, 0–100 (100 = fully open) | | `aq <air conditioner> mode cool` | `auto`, `heat`, `cool`, `dry`, or `fan` | | `aq <air conditioner> temp 24` | Temperature in Celsius, 18–30 | | `aq scene <search>` | Search saved scenes; Return requests execution | | `aq update` | Refresh homes, devices, and scenes for the current account | | `aq home` / `aq homes` | Switch between homes across all saved accounts and regions | | `aq home <search>` | Filter homes by home name or account label | | `aq home update` | Discover homes across every saved account | | `aq account` | List saved accounts and regions; select one to restore its last home | | `aq account add <name>` | Save another account/region's API key in a secure dialog | | `aq account rename` | Choose any saved account and enter its new name in a dialog | | `aq account rename <name>` | Rename the current account profile | | `aq showstatus on` / `off` | Automatically show live state on device selection; default off | | `aq login` | Open Aqara's sign-in page | | `aq apikey` | Replace the current account's API key using a secure dialog | | `aq reinit` | Delete all saved accounts, credentials, home selections, and catalogs |
If a device has the same name as a workflow command, use `aq device <name>`. Devices with duplicate names include room labels; select the exact result to choose a particular device. Multi-channel products may appear as several separately controllable devices.
## Multiple homes, accounts, and regions
`aq home` lists every discovered home across all saved accounts. The current home is marked, and each result includes its account label. Select a home to switch; the workflow remembers that choice. The first result under `aq` shows your current account and home and opens the home picker.
All homes exposed by one account/region share its API key. To connect another account or region:
1. Optionally name the existing connection with `aq account rename Personal`. 2. Run `aq login` and sign in to Aqara Agent with the other account, choosing the region that matches its homes in Aqara Home. Copy its `aqara_api_key`. 3. Run `aq account add US` (or any name you prefer) and paste the key in the secure dialog. The workflow validates it and discovers all homes it exposes. 4. Use `aq home` to choose among homes from both connections. For example, `aq home US` filters by the saved account label.
Each account keeps its own credential, remembered home, device and scene catalogs, and status cache. Switching back to a previously loaded home restores its catalog immediately; use `aq update` to refresh it. A home being selected for the first time loads its catalog from Aqara. Controls and scenes remain scoped to the account and home where they were selected. Homes without saved scenes are supported. If loading a new home's catalog fails, the previous selection and cached data are restored.
To rename a connection that cannot currently load, use `aq account rename`, select that account, and enter a new display name. Renaming does not require switching to that account or contacting Aqara. Account names should contain only a label such as `Work` or `Personal`; API keys go in the separate secure dialog.
Use `aq home update` to discover newly added homes across all saved accounts. Replacing a key with `aq apikey` clears only that connection's home selection and catalogs. Adding another connection preserves the existing connections.
Controls are offered by device family. A specific light may lack color or color temperature support; Aqara can reject a command the hardware does not support. Aqara Agent [explicitly excludes door lock lock/unlock commands](https://github.com/aqara/aqara-agent-skills/blob/main/skills/aqara-agent/SKILL.md#out-of-scope). Door locks therefore show status and an explanation of the unavailable controls. The current API action table also does not document hub security mode controls. Lock control would require a separate supported connection, such as Apple Home or Home Assistant. Lock and unlock are never guessed or sent through the generic Aqara device control API. Serialized device status is displayed as readable fields joined in the device's subtitle, for example: `Door: Closed · Lock: Locked · Connection: Online`. Internal remote-control flags are hidden. Copy or Large Type on a status row shows the full summary when the subtitle is too long to fit. Notifications describe the requested action, such as “Turning Desk Light on” or “Setting Desk Light to 50% brightness.” Use `status` to check the device's resulting state. Commands are never retried automatically after a timeout, since they may already have been executed by Aqara.
## Local data
API keys are generic passwords in macOS Keychain with service `com.schwark.aqara`. The original connection uses account `api-key`; added connections use `api-key:<profile-id>`. Home selections and catalogs are stored in Alfred's workflow data directory, outside the installed workflow:
```text ~/Library/Application Support/Alfred/Workflow Data/com.schwark.aqara/ ```
Search uses the local catalog, so typing does not repeatedly query the API. The original connection retains its existing files. Added connections have separate data directories under `profiles/<profile-id>/`; `accounts.json` stores their labels and the active profile, with no credentials. Run `aq update` when adding, removing, or renaming devices or scenes. Status requests are cached for five seconds. Controls, scene requests, home changes, and reconnection invalidate status. Replacing the key clears the previous connection's catalogs and home selection. A failed catalog refresh keeps the prior catalog unless the selected home is no longer available.
If `aq update` reports **NoHomesUnderAccount**, Aqara Agent is not returning any homes for the saved credential. Check that the M3 appears in Aqara Home under the same account and region used when signing in to Aqara Agent. Then use `aq login` and `aq apikey` to reconnect. Workflow errors identify the failed operation and known account problems without displaying raw server messages or credentials. Errors appear in Alfred's workflow debugger as well as its notifications.
## Development
```sh python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v python3 workflow-build ```
The workflow runner finds Python in the standard Apple Silicon Homebrew, Intel Homebrew/python.org, and system locations without depending on a shell profile. The build uses an explicit file allowlist and excludes local data, tests, `.git`, and credentials. Both macOS's Python 3.9 and current Homebrew Python are supported.
`filter.py` renders Alfred results, `command.py` executes selected actions, `common.py` manages Aqara requests and the catalog, and `keychain.py` uses the native Security framework. API requests are fixed to the official HTTPS host; redirects are rejected so the bearer key is not forwarded elsewhere.
## API references
The workflow icon is Aqara's logo, sourced from its [official GitHub organization](https://github.com/aqara).
